searchText: I've made a Kurtosis config with Lodestar and Geth: https://github.com/jihoonsong/local-devnet-bals/blob/main/kurtosis.config.registry.yaml It seems Geth doesn't support the latest engine APIs change? Lodestar wants to use `engine_getPayloadV6` but Geth doesn't have it yet. cc <@427903869226582018> whoops. I've pushed it to the branch now <@845691100072509460> where is the branch located that I would be able to use to build the lodestar image? or can you build it and push it to a registry? Thanks! At slot 32 (the first slot of Gloas), Lodestar produces an error as follow: ``` [cl-1-lodestar-geth] Sep-19 06:42:44.134[api] warn: Engine failed to produce the block slot=32, parentSlot=31, parentBlockRoot=0x2d3945c73f4a543c3dec777fc8ee9ed622e9edf14c716015779cb4121a35792f, fork=gloas, builderSelection=executiononly, isBuilderEnabled=false, isEngineEnabled=true, strictFeeRecipientCheck=false, builderBoostFactor=0, durationMs=19 - blockAccessList missing for gloas >= gloas executionPayload number=32 hash=0xbccbc92ec7368b08588ccc0873d98db8cba3e3ab5aa9bab2fb541d67f773946e [cl-1-lodestar-geth] Error: blockAccessList missing for gloas >= gloas executionPayload number=32 hash=0xbccbc92ec7368b08588ccc0873d98db8cba3e3ab5aa9bab2fb541d67f773946e [cl-1-lodestar-geth] at parseExecutionPayload (file:///usr/app/packages/beacon-node/src/execution/engine/types.ts:394:13) [cl-1-lodestar-geth] at ExecutionEngineHttp.getPayload (file:///usr/app/packages/beacon-node/src/execution/engine/http.ts:466:12) ``` oh it's right above You can build the Lodestar image based on this [branch](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/8426) or can use this one "jihoonsg/lodestar-eip7928:941c102" <@427903869226582018> I saw that you want to use Amsterdam time, which ethereum-package doesn't support at the moment. Let me make it work for you :) sgtm! I just fixed the issue with RLP decoding of BALs and pushed it to my Geth branch. I'd suggest to rebuild the image based on the changes. Like I said earlier, probably this issue/fix has no relevance to the devnet use-case, but might as well test against the fix just to be safe. Nice! But it looks like Geth still returns empty BALs. Maybe `BlockToExecutableData()` needs to set `BlockAccessList` field? appears so do you have a patch for kurtosis? ~~I've opened a [PR](https://github.com/ethpandaops/ethereum-package/pull/1187) but in the meantime, you could use "github.com/jihoonsong/ethereum-package@eip7928". For instance, this Kurtosis command is good: `kurtosis run github.com/jihoonsong/ethereum-package@eip7928 --enclave eip7928 --args-file ./eip7928.yaml`~~ (This is not needed at all. I was confused with the Lodestar's timestamp issue below. Feel free to ignore this.) ~~Wait, please don't rely on it yet. I'm testing it and it seems it's not done.~~ It turned out the issue was something else. It's good to use If there’s no kurtosis package changes, please feel free to add it to the tests folder under .github with .norun at the file ending. We collect all examples there! Sounds great! Could you give me a pointer where to put it? It seems there is no .yaml.norun example under .github folder Eg: https://github.com/ethpandaops/ethereum-package/blob/main/.github/tests/mainnet-split.yaml.norun I've opened a PR to your branch that uses Amsterdam time and PayloadV4. Please have a look when you have some time: https://github.com/jwasinger/go-ethereum/pull/16 When calling `forkchoiceUpdatedV3`, does Lodestar set `params.timestamp` to parent block's time? i.e., at the first slot of Gloas, `params.timestamp` equals to the timestamp of the last slot of Fulu (when there is no missed slot). This makes Geth think it's still in Osaka when it just entered Gloas. Thanks! Let me add some config once we have a working combination. I'm also getting the same as Jihoon describes. Geth needs to be updated to support engine_getPayloadV6 for the EIP-7928/Gloas fork, correct? `engine_getPayloadV6` should be supported now. did you try it recently? also, are you using prysm? what does your testing workflow look like? FYI, Prysm doesn't work at the moment. Let me share a Kurtosis config with Prysm soon. should this be checking for V6: ``` func (api *ConsensusAPI) GetPayloadV6(payloadID engine.PayloadID) (*engine.ExecutionPayloadEnvelope, error) { if !payloadID.Is(engine.PayloadV4) { return nil, engine.UnsupportedFork } return api.getPayload(payloadID, false) } ``` using lodestar we use the state slot and since we call `forkchoiceUpdatedV3` with payload attributes in previous slot it will be fulu timestamp since technically it's still fulu Do you mean `if !payloadID.Is(engine.PayloadV4)`? If so, that's for `ExecutionPayloadV4` so I believe it's correct. Right, so the first Gloas block (when there is no missed slot) won't have BALs, which would be fine. I think we can update Geth to return BALs and see if there is any remaining issue. In the meantime, I'll be working on making Prysm interop happen. the problem with this at least right now is that we call `engine_getPayloadV6` for gloas slot 0 and if there is no `blockAccessList` we reject the payload (btw, I 'm running a BAL import benchmark on my dev machine but I plan to test out the lodestar/geth local devnet setup once the benchmark finishes) Very nice, it seems we're all on the same page btw regarding this, there was similar case with deneb since we added `blobGasUsed` and `excessBlobGas` to execution payload RPC response, so might be worth checking how that was handled by EL Thanks for sharing! Let me study it tomorrow 👍 When a transaction aborts due to an`INVALID` or `REVERT` operation, will BAL be empty? what is an `INVALID`? https://www.evm.codes/?fork=cancun#fe `0xfe` opcode if the transaction is valid for inclusion in the block at its index, regardless of how it terminates its execution the referenced state should be in the BAL actually wait... the state is reverted upon failure Any storage/account reads would still be in the BAL and the tx sender fee payment to coinbase. That's all. We should make this explicit in the specs <@792404665068158998> Agree for coinbase (state change) . What is the rationale behind adding reads / touched accounts in BAL? what do you mean exactly, could you elaborate? there is a point on exceptional halts in the eip Or something like "if a call reverts, record the addresses and storage keys as if they were read" Alice calls a `Contract` which does an `SLOAD(0x01)`, checks `BALANCE` for another account say Bob, does `SSTORE(0x02,0x03)` and aborts via `REVERT` / `INVALID`. Will BAL include 1. `Contract` in `account_changes`? 1. If so will it contain the storage read / write? 2. `Bob` in `account_changes`? 1) yes 1.1) will contain 2 reads ( 0x01, 0x02) 2) yes Great scenario! We should definitely have that covered in the test One could argue we have it in the EIP already: ``` Accessed but unchanged: Include the address with empty changes (e.g., targets of EXTCODEHASH, EXTCODESIZE, BALANCE, STATICCALL, etc.). ``` But will make it more explicit! 👋 if you can share the config, i can quickly debug and make it work on my end, shouldn't take too long
